title: Make Every Value Share Parity
statement:
You get an array nums of distinct positive integers. Build a new array out of the same length. For every index i you choose one of two options on its own:

  • keep it: out[i] = nums[i], or
  • subtract another entry: out[i] = nums[i] − nums[j] for any index j ≠ i of the original array. The result may be zero or negative.

Return true if you can make every value of out even, or every value of out odd. Otherwise return false.

examples.why: Keep 3 (odd) and turn 8 into 8 − 3 = 5 (odd). All odd.
Everything is already even, so keep every value.
Mixed parities. Aim for odd: 1 and 9 stay, 6 becomes 6 − 1 = 5 and 4 becomes 4 − 9 = −5. A negative result is allowed.

hints: Subtracting changes parity in a predictable way. Odd minus odd, odd minus even, even minus odd: which of these are odd?
Try to make everything odd. Which values already work, and which values need a subtraction? What must exist in the array for that subtraction to help?
If the array has at least one odd value, every even value can subtract it and become odd. If it has no odd value, everything is already even. Is there any case left?

explain.intuition:
The puzzle looks like a search over choices, but parity rules settle it. An even number minus an odd number is odd. So if nums holds at least one odd value, aim for "all odd": odd values stay as they are, and each even value subtracts that odd value (it is a different index, since it has a different parity). If nums holds no odd value, every entry is already even and you keep them all.

Those two cases cover every possible array, so the answer is always true. The lesson for interviews: before writing a search, check whether a simple invariant decides the answer outright. The brute force below is still useful as a way to convince yourself.
steps: Count whether any value is odd.
If yes, the target parity is odd: odd values are kept, even values subtract an odd value.
If no, the target parity is even: every value is kept.
Either way a valid out exists, so return true.
pitfalls: Returning false just because the input mixes parities. Mixed input is exactly when the subtraction is useful.
Aiming for "all even" with mixed input: an odd value minus an odd value is even, but only if there is a second odd value. A lone odd value cannot become even, so pick the odd target instead.

solutions.title: Check each target parity directly
solutions.idea: For each target parity, check that every index either already has it or can reach it by subtracting some other entry.

solutions.title: Parity argument
solutions.idea: With any odd value present, every even value minus that odd value is odd. With no odd value, everything is already even. So a solution always exists.

followups: Now the subtraction is allowed only when nums[j] < nums[i], so the result stays positive. When can the answer be false?
Return an actual out array instead of true or false.
